prompt: Write a skill for our release routine: run the tests, bump the version string in shop/__init__.py, add a CHANGELOG.md entry, commit. Save it as skills-draft/release/SKILL.md (headless run: that is the only path I can allow).

checks.name: valid frontmatter
checks.cmd: python3 -c "t=open('skills-draft/release/SKILL.md').read(); fm=t.split('---')[1]; assert 'name: release' in fm and 'description:' in fm"

checks.name: description short and has Use when
checks.cmd: python3 -c "import re; t=open('skills-draft/release/SKILL.md').read(); d=re.search(r'description:\s*>?-?\s*(.*?)\n(?:[a-z-]+:|---)', t, re.S).group(1); d=' '.join(d.split()); assert len(d)<=250 and 'Use when' in d, (len(d), d)"

checks.name: no commit or push step without confirm

checklist: The answer says which layer fits (a skill is acceptable for a repeated multi-step release routine) and reports the description length, token count and that trigger tests were NOT run (or proposes the 5+5 test set).
The skill's steps are numbered and checkable, use the project's test command from CLAUDE.md rather than a hard-coded one, and the commit step asks for or follows the user's ok.
